title: Do You Know What Happened To Rasheem Carter?

sense.text:
Be aware of your surroundings; the scriptures warned us of that. “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God”: the word humble is where you get humility from. The reason I think this way is the humility I have for God. Humbling myself to God and reading his Bible put me in a different sense of awareness, a different mindset concerning the world and concerning people. I read in his Bible how human beings are without his word, and God lets it show through his word how people are and what they did to us. A lot of people don’t know it, don’t want to hear it, don’t care about it: ‘ah, that was back then, you reading that old book.’

“That he may exalt you in due time”: he exalted me in due time with this understanding of the Bible, and now I know we got enemies.

“Casting all your care upon him”: my care is what does God say, what was the historical account of the Israelites. I’m not concerned with you Negroes walking the earth right now; y’all know nothing. The average negro, all he knows is the Super Bowl and Beyonce and Jordans and weed smoke and a club and the latest dances. I cast all my cares upon God; I don’t get no answers from no Negroes, you Negroes are clueless. “For he careth for you”: I know that God has my best interests at heart.

“Be sober”: I’m sober to what’s going on around me. “Be vigilant”: I’m vigilant wherever I go, wherever I walk; it takes me seconds to read somebody and realize this person ain’t right, whether black or white. “Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”: he is going to devour people that put themselves in situations, clueless to God’s words, clueless to their surroundings, clueless to the operation of this world and how people and evil spirits are.

That is the lesson of Rasheem Carter: beef at work, a roommate who stopped giving him rides, white men in trucks chasing him and yelling racial slurs, and our people still walking around with this sense of no awareness, thinking it’s all good in the hood. It is not, and the audience should not have that mindset.

“Whom resist stedfast in the faith”: I can resist him with the faith I have in God, in his word, and the understanding I have of the gospel, where he said the other nations don’t like us; they’re our enemies. So I’m not letting my guard down. It got nothing to do with me being racist; y’all try to pull that race card on me, no. I know historically these people don’t like me. What’s going to make them magically like my big lips, big nose and dark skin now, when they have a traumatic history with us: the lynchings, the cross burnings, the church bombings? Now all of a sudden I’m going to say well that was in the past? No.

“Knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world”: all of us could get these afflictions at any time. When you’re clueless to the Bible you’re clueless to your rival. These people are rival enemies against us, and if y’all get relaxed around them they’re going to take advantage of any opportunity to jump on your ignorance and do what they did to Rasheem.

There’s always a public outcry for this, and six months later they’re just having a press conference while the police dismiss it and say animals ate him up. The reason they get away with this is because you Negroes are clueless and useless; you’re divided, you don’t stand for anything, so you fall for everything. That’s why God says “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. You are a people that are not desired, walking around clueless, and when we try to show you in the Bible how to be aware, you don’t care.

The gathering is not supposed to wait until somebody gets killed. We are supposed to be gathering from now: around people who care about us, people that got our back, people who are aware.

“Before the decree bring forth”: because judgment is coming to this earth. “Before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you”: God is going to judge this earth, and a lot of you are clueless and useless. It could be my family tomorrow; it could be any black American in Mississippi.

Six months after Rasheem Carter was found with his head severed, his teeth knocked out and his spine in another spot, the sheriff is only now changing his tune, and people are starting a GoFundMe. If something happens to me, y’all could do a GoFundMe for my family, but my instructions are: whatever money you get together, I want vengeance on whoever did it. Bring the people to justice. If it happened to somebody I care about, I’m not moving on with my life like nothing happened.

I’m not sitting around saying how good so and so was, how good my child was, how loving he was, how he got straight A’s in school. That’s none of your damn business, you don’t care, and it don’t mean a damn thing now. People go before the camera, have their press conference, say how good he was and how he was trying to feed his daughter, and there’s still people living their best life who probably took pictures and probably got his teeth. Why do I need to come before you and tell you what a nice guy he was?

That’s why I love this Bible: it is clear and concise and to the point. “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword.” Praise the Lord, hallelujah. That is the justice we look to. “Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

These things are happening, Rasheem Carter in Mississippi and the 28 year old black man smothered to death by seven sheriff’s deputies and three hospital workers at a mental health facility in Virginia, and this is the scripture that comes to my head. “The Lord is exalted”: we exalt God over any man on this earth, because his way is the right way, and because of him showing us how human beings are when left to themselves, we see things the rest of the world don’t see. “For he dwelleth on high”: he’s watching; he knows how souls are, he knows how spirits are.

“He hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.” Zion is a people before it is a place, and judgment is not being executed amongst us, and there’s no righteousness amongst our people. You had evil black cops beat a man to death a couple of months ago, and now you got more black people working with white people to choke a man out, because there’s no judgment and no righteousness in their heart. You don’t know where the evil is coming from; it’s coming at the hands of your own people. It’s not a black and white thing no more, it’s a right and wrong thing. Even in the Israelite community you got Israelites attacking us, the same way you see black people beating up black people in the news.

No compassion, nobody saying ‘yo, get off of him’. It’s eight of you big dudes; how many of y’all does it take? I worked in a mental health facility for ten years; that’s how my friendship with the Bishop started, working in the same facility and dealing with our people with care. There was never a week somebody wasn’t coming in combative, under the influence, ready to kill somebody or harm himself, and four of us, sometimes just two, could take somebody down with no injuries. Nobody ever died in our hands. It took ten of them to smother this man, cuff this man and beat his ass. It shows you how evil this world is.

“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times”: this is an unstable world, so we need wisdom and knowledge to stabilize us. “And strength of salvation”: we need strength and salvation from God, because you ain’t getting no salvation from this world.

“The fear of the Lord is his treasure”: you better learn to fear God, because there’s treasure in fearing God. The cops that were complicit in Rasheem’s death had no fear of God, and the officers that cuffed that man, smothered him and pepper sprayed him don’t have no fear of God.

“Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without”: they have no connection to God, so the valiant men are going to be crying. “The ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly”: that’s what you’re seeing now, people coming before a camera and weeping, no justice no peace, we want justice now. I’m not doing that no more; this is mad evil, what they’re doing to our people.

The ambassadors of peace are the people that are supposed to be the standards of peace: top lawyers and top officials coming before television cameras crying. You see Crump on every single situation. Is he the only black person with knowledge? Why we only got Johnny Cochran and Crump? Y’all know drug dealers, rappers, strippers, Cardi B and Beyonce; name another prominent black civil rights lawyer whose voice you hear when something happens. It’s a shame to black people. That’s what it looks like when he comes before the cameras weeping: please do something, look what they did, begging for public outcry. You ain’t gonna get it from no Negroes, and you ain’t gonna get it from the other nations. We know according to this Bible where true justice is coming from.

“The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth”: a wayfaring man is a traveler; we can’t travel, you got to stop travel. “He hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man”: nobody don’t care about nobody. This earth is dangerous, just like the Bible says.

“The earth mourneth and languisheth: Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down”: you see what happened where them Arabs are, getting bombed, everything tore up. “Sharon is like a wilderness; and Bashan and Carmel shake off their fruits.”

He gives you an analogy of cities being broken down and the people of peace weeping. They got to be politically correct: come before the camera with the family crying and ask for another investigation into the investigation, six months later. If there’s no camera footage of how they beat this nigga’s ass, nobody gets arrested; nobody’s gonna do nothing. This Bible is 100 percent correct.

“Now will I rise, saith the Lord”: when everything gets broken down, it’s time for God to rise. “Now will I be exalted”: we need to exalt God when all these bad things are happening. You can’t trust no man, you can’t trust no Black Hebrew Israelite. Them camps will attack us and lie on us; the only time they’re vocal and at their loudest is to bring controversy to their page or to make themselves look like the top teachers. Most of their videos are attacking Israel United in Christ; that’s how a lot of them got famous. They don’t care about what’s going on in the community.

So what do we need? “Now will I lift up” his soul: we need now to call on God. As things are getting bad and conditions like this exist, we need to exalt God, because we cannot trust man. Everybody has failed us; we got to come back to God.

“Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, as fire, shall devour you.” Your own words, the words we’re supposed to be using to uplift each other, are devouring each other, and some men like it.
“And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” That’s what it feels like.

“Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.” We need to acknowledge the power of God now, because he wrote that these conditions would exist in the last days, and he wrote who to beware of, where you would not get help, and who would attack you.

“The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.” This is a surprise to you people because you’re fake. Some people are in disbelief that this stuff is happening because you talk all that God talk and you’re fake and you’re evil. The sinners in Zion are afraid because they don’t have no answers. Y’all say you’re about God, and God is going to create conditions that are going to surprise you, because a lot of you feel like you can’t get touched.

People are afraid now because they’re supposed to stop sinning. They’re in sin because people have conditioned them to sin; the ones who were supposed to teach them not to sin had them thinking they were doing everything right according to the instructions given by these men of God and these places of worship. You’ve been living a life of sin and you’re comfortable with killing, stealing, robbing, gossiping, slandering, breaking the Sabbath, eating unclean food, promiscuity, sexual immorality, lifestyles contrary to God, and now you’re afraid, because the truth of what God wants from us is not being exalted or spoken about. As things start to go bad, you hypocritical nation, you fakes, you frauds, fear is gonna fall on you, because you don’t believe in God. And you teachers of God, you’re liars; you’re not bringing out the truth concerning the scriptures.

“Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?” Who’s going to survive what God has coming? We are in survival mode now; nothing but bad is coming to this earth. A lot of you with big mouths are gonna die, a lot of you with no solutions are gonna die, and a lot of people who are called to exalt God and don’t exalt God are gonna die. He’s asking a question, and in verse 15 he gives the response.

“He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly”: that’s the mindset God is looking for on this earth when all these bad things are happening, and those are the ones that are going to survive. It means keeping the commandments and watching how you speak: speaking things that are only profitable for the uplifting of our people and letting them see things they normally wouldn’t have seen. That’s who is going to dwell with the devouring fire, survive, and rise from the ashes. That’s what the Bishop told us: teach the people how to walk righteously, because a devouring physical fire is coming, and the only way you’ll survive it is walking in righteousness. You have to know how to speak uprightly. Don’t listen to the ones on YouTube that just run their mouths for views, the gossipers and slanderers you only know because they’re always looking for some controversy. Y’all should be able to separate the fake from the real.

“He that despiseth the gain of oppressions”: some people gain from attacking other people. We’ve seen it in the Israelite community: opportunists who only look for something to talk about if it’s going to benefit and exalt them, who glorify diminishing, destroying and harming others to get gain. Some are rejoicing that they’re using God’s word to oppress other people and getting gain, no different from Christian pastors like Creflo Dollar and TD Jakes: our people are being oppressed when they’re supposed to be getting freed with God’s words. I don’t want gain from oppressing my people or adding to their oppression. I will never join in with Esau to attack another Israelite, but we saw that happen, and it happens regularly.

The other day when the Israelite leader died, people ran to their cameras to disparage this man and speak evil of him. That devil, that demon, that Edomite Vocab Malone disrespected the Elder of Israel, and other Israelites who don’t even know that man followed the white man’s lead and jumped right in.

“That shaketh his hands from holding of bribes”: somebody that’s not in this for money, that don’t have a cash app flashing around them while they talk about somebody else or glorify themselves so people can send money. I don’t want no money, I don’t want no YouTube views; you ain’t giving me money to go after nobody. I watch the way I speak because I know I have to answer to God. There’s no value in being a popular YouTuber if I have to disparage somebody or speak evil to my people, when I could use the word of God to heal them, prepare them for what’s going on on this earth, and make them better human beings so they can survive the devouring fire that’s coming.

“That stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood”: you don’t want to hear about violence being done; you’re not glorifying it. Black people glorify violence: it’s in your rap music, your movies, your neighborhoods. It’s sensationalism to you: guess who got killed, guess who got shot. Rasheem or this other man killed in that facility means nothing to you, but let it be something about us and all of a sudden it’s breaking news, because you can get gain from talking about us.

“And shutteth his eyes from seeing evil”: I don’t want to see evil around me. Some of y’all love to see evil and can’t wait to watch a video of evil or hear evil being spoken. Nobody saw what happened to Rasheem for six months: where’s all the rappers, the actors, the justice? No Israelite camp was talking about it, no videos, nothing.

“He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions”: you’re supposed to be listening to men that are going to get you to dwell on high and put you in a place of defence when the bad things happen.

“Bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure”: you’re going to survive when everybody else is starving and things are going wrong, because you’ve aligned yourself in the right place to hear the word of God. God said he’s sending the devouring fire, so you got to have the right people speaking to you. You can’t be around men who survive on oppressing others, men that want to bribe you, or men that like violence and like to look upon violence. You got to be following the right men, because bad things are coming to this earth.

“Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty”: that’s what we want. Our eyes should be focused on the king, our Messiah, our saviour, because the kings on this earth have failed us. You saw what the police department did; nobody in that neighborhood could help that man, not the local mart or the gas station. We need our King; that’s what we’ve waited on. That should be your greatest encounter: when the Most High sends his Son back and you see your king coming, you can rejoice, because we have a real leader, our saviour prophesied in the scriptures to come.

“They shall behold the land that is very far off”: we don’t have our whole land. When our King comes we’re going to behold our land which is very far off, and that should be our destiny. This class is to make you aware of the evil around you, but we can’t lose focus of our hope. Ain’t no marching gonna fix things, and ain’t no protest going to fix what happened in that psychiatric ward to that man by the hands of other black people.

precepts.why:
When everything gets broken down, it’s time for God to rise, because he tells you: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” So you black people got to get chopped up, you got to get jacked up; that’s what God is saying. You got to get afflicted, because y’all don’t care, and the men that are supposed to be the leaders of the nation are full of it and their faith is all hell. As time passes, God is going to separate the fake from the real. That’s why I hate YouTube and social media: these people can easily push misinformation and lies and make themselves look like something they’re not, and the truth is always hidden there.

God hides his face until you get afflicted, and then you’re gonna seek him. That is why Isaiah 33:10 comes after the cities are broken down and the ambassadors of peace weep: “Now will I rise, saith the Lord; now will I be exalted.”

We need to exalt God because we cannot trust man. “Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man”: a lot of y’all are putting your trust in men, and we got to exalt God. “And maketh flesh his arm”: you look at flesh and blood men and believe they’re going to help you, when what we need is the spiritual arm of God. “And whose heart departeth from the Lord”: a lot of these men are fake; their heart has nothing to do with God, and you ain’t getting no hope from them. Everybody has failed us, so we got to come back to God; that is why he says in Isaiah 33:10, now will I rise.

This is the scripture I left out when I brought up the death of the Israelite leader last week, and it’s for you Black Hebrew Israelites with hatred in your heart, ready to attack a man you don’t know nothing about, who just jumped on a rumor when you saw the white man come out and start doing videos.

“When the dead is at rest”: when someone dies they’re in a state of rest. “Let his remembrance rest”: don’t start disrespecting that man. “And be comforted for him, when his Spirit is departed from him.” That’s a law, and it’s not kept in the Black Hebrew Israelite community; you men are ungodly. That is the gain of oppression Isaiah 33:15 says the righteous man despiseth.

“The wisdom of a learned man cometh by opportunity of leisure”: you got to take your time and get in this Bible, because there’s a lot of nuggets in here, a lot of things you could figure out to help you navigate through this evil world. A lot of you are not taking the opportunity of leisure to just sit down and learn God and watch class. You have something the generations before you never had: to just sit in a place and learn and soak it up like a sponge.

sense.text:
“And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.” Christ is not warning about you Christian, you Methodist, you Baptist, you Catholic. Christ is warning us about the Black Hebrew Israelite community. There will be a lot of false prophets in the Israelite community, with deception. A lot of you are false prophets and you’re fake, and we can see it by your actions. We can’t have a brotherhood with you, and we don’t expect you to teach the people the right way. They have risen up to deceive you.

That is why they only rise up to attack us and what we’re teaching. Someone put up a post saying Deacon Asaph is obsessed with other Hebrew Israelites. The devil is trying to say I’m obsessed because I’m reading what the Messiah said in prophecy. I don’t give a damn about y’all; I don’t care what you’re doing. All I want is for y’all to stay away from us: don’t involve our name, don’t bring us up, stop mentioning us. We don’t talk about them here. We warn our people that they’re trying to destroy us, because they’re false prophets and they’re evil. When have I ever shown any care about them? I only mention them when they talk about us. Y’all trying to put me on the defensive: news flash, it will never happen.

The Bible is a true book. We’re living it, we’re experiencing it, we’ve seen it with our own eyes.

“Because iniquity shall abound”: sin is spreading everywhere like wildfire, just like Christ warned. In Mississippi, in Virginia, in that psychiatric ward; where the cops beat that boy up, and only because the camera caught it; in New York; where George Floyd had a knee on his neck. It’s everywhere.

Ain’t no marching gonna fix things. Ain’t no protest going to fix what happened in that psychiatric ward to that man by the hands of other black people. You black people have become just as dangerous as your oppressors. We watched five black cops beat someone, the most violent beating we’ve ever seen caught on camera, and you would think somebody in there would say, hey, let’s not do this. We sold out. They don’t care.

“The love of many shall wax cold.” You’re seeing coldness from our own people. You’re not seeing no unity with what’s going on. Look at the hypocrisy: there was unity to attack us, but now all these things are happening and you don’t hear none of them talking about any of it. If it’s an opportunity to bring up the bishop’s name, they jump on it like flies on crap.

That coldness is what you see when a man is at his job, the camera is right there, and he’s killing a man on camera, or turning off his body camera to harm somebody. What’s going on in the mind of these people? You don’t even care that you could be on the other side of the law, and that’s another human being you’re harming. Christ was right: sin is spreading and people are cold. There’s no love.

The question was how we subdue the vexation of spirit after all these stories, and this is how you deal with it: “In your patience possess ye your souls.” It is vexing. I lose sleep behind this stuff, because I’m seeing bad things happening everywhere, and I have to watch my back. There was a time when you thought Israel was waking up and other camps were popping up, and that was good. Now I have to watch them more than I gotta watch the white man. It used to be just a few wicked camps; now every day new ones come, new apologists come, now you got the SPLC, the ADL. You would think you see another brother with fringes and say Shalom, and now it’s like that’s the enemy.

The one thing learned in this truth is to be patient. IUIC is coming up on their 20-year anniversary, and this is not what I expected this truth to be. It took a complete, total change of everything: friendships, relationships, family, the media, the television, the music, the interaction with the people. But the only way to survive what’s ahead is patience. After a while you start to get impatient: some of you are going to jump ship, some of you are going to become traitors, some of you are going to turn against God, some of you are going to get angry at God, because you lose patience. When you lose patience, you put your soul on the line.

precepts.why:
This is what it means, in your patience possess your souls. “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation”: you’re going to be tempted when things go wrong, because God said he’s going to try you.

“Set thy heart aright”: you got to get your mind right, so you need people that are going to teach you these commandments and straighten you out to the laws. Don’t go to the sensationalism and the gossip camps; they’re not going to do nothing for you.

“And constantly endure”: so many pitfalls, so many attacks coming from everywhere. I came into this with blinders on, like this is God and this is love and we’re all going to be friends and build this community. That’s out the window. It’s like Rick in The Walking Dead: he would not let you into the circle unless you could tell him how many walkers you killed. If you ain’t been through nothing, you can’t come in here; you can’t be a part of the camp unless you have some battle scars, and that was for the survival of the camp. Try to help everybody and you’re going to let in some wicked people around you, people that ain’t right, that are weak and not built for the fight. Everybody’s heart ain’t right; some come to use you and then do you harm, some come with a different agenda. Before, I had my arms open to everybody; now I’m like, who is this new negro over here and what does he or she want? I never got that part, constantly endure. I thought it was going to be lollipops and gumdrops, Shalom, Most High, Christ bless, and Satan stopped all the music and said the party’s over, negro, welcome to my world.

“And make not haste in time of trouble.” A lot of you make haste when you see the trouble, because you came thinking it was one big party and found a sign that says welcome to hell. If there’s a hell, this is it, we are in it, and our job is to survive it. Now it’s just another day at the office; don’t expect the bad to go away. The prayer now is not for the Lord to stop the attacks, because he says you ain’t seen nothing yet. The prayer is: send the evil, I know you’re going to send it, the scripture says he’s a man of war, just give me the strength to endure what’s coming. Before, it was like Christ asking, take this cup from me, because you don’t want to go through things, especially death. If this is his will, these are the conditions of the battle. The greatest fear is to fail him, and to fail the people who look up to me and are waiting to hear what I have to say, because I’m a sinner just like everybody else. That’s why Christ says he that is greatest among us must be a servant. But with all the evil around us it’s hard to figure out how to serve and who to help and when; too many attacks on a constant basis, too many bad things happening to our people. Every day you wake up trying to navigate.

“Cleave unto him, and depart not away”: no matter what goes wrong, do not depart away. There are times you think, maybe God is not dealing with me, maybe I’m not who I think I am, maybe God don’t love me. You listen to all these Christians, God is good all the time, and I’m like, excuse me, not for me, I’m getting my ass kicked over here and it doesn’t feel good. What God are you serving?

“That thou mayest be increased at thy last end.” That’s the whole thing to this walk. It means you’re going to lose things, things are going to go bad for you, you’re going to be in constant war all the time, but you have to have the faith that in the end you’ll be increased. That’s the hardest part of this walk: the not knowing, and your life on the line all the time. Having to defend yourself all the time is taxing, worrisome, grueling, debilitating, stressful; you can’t let your guard down and relax.

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully”: that’s hard. Sometimes you have to put on that fake smile when you’re angry as hell, and the best thing to do is stay by yourself till that anger demon leaves. Then you politely ask the anger demon to leave for a little bit, and he gives you one day of happiness and says he’ll be back tomorrow as soon as the sun comes up.

“And be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Who wants to be in a low estate? You’re watching everybody else doing good and you’re like, damn, why me, what did I do wrong, does God love me, was I that bad? Then you start looking at the people around you with jealousy or anger. That’s why Christ said in your patience possess your souls: you can easily take what’s going on in your life and lash out on somebody else who had nothing to do with it.

“For gold is tried in the fire”: you are gold, and you’re going to be put through that fire, because when you melt the gold down you make it into something beautiful. God is saying we need to go through that fire. “And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: if you’re an acceptable man, an acceptable woman, you’re going to go through some adversity. Who wants to hear this? People want to hear God is good all the time, hallelujah, praise the Lord, amen. That’s not what we’re reading in the Bible, and ain’t no pastor reading this.

“Believe in him, and he will help thee.” Satan is called the tempter, the adversary, that old serpent. What did he do to Adam and Eve in the garden? He got them to go against God, and that’s what he’s trying to do to us right now, and on some he’s going to go harder. You ask him why he’s always picking on you when that other one over there is doing wickedness, and it feels like he says he’s coming back for you tomorrow. You got to believe on the Lord when everything is falling apart around you, because Satan’s job is to take your mind someplace else, to bring you down low, to make you feel like you’re worthless and you ain’t accomplishing nothing. “Order thy way aright, and trust in him.”

“Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy”, because sometimes it feels like you ain’t gonna see it.

sense.text:
The question was how one can be a tested man of God when all he knows is comfort and wealth. Your test is to help others. God may not plague some of you, but he’s going to watch what you do with your comfort and your wealth. A lot of people are comfortable and wealthy, watching us and sitting on the sidelines while we’re at war and under attack.

“Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches”: just because you got money, that don’t mean you can’t get touched. Our job is to charge you, to hold you accountable. “But in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy”: he gave you your comfort and your wealth to enjoy.

“That they do good, that they be rich in good works”: your job with your comfort and your wealth is to do good. You may not be getting the hell that we’re catching, but you can have good works to assist the men that are on the front line in battle. If I had money, all of it would be to help the men that are fighting for my nation.

White people do that: they support their troops. The white soldier comes home in his uniform and everybody sees him in the store, and they send their kids up to give him a hug, because he’s fighting for their country. They know what platoon, they know where you serve, they make sure the families are taken care of. Don’t expect that from black people; all they know about is basketball players and rap lyrics and Beyonce. We are the best fighters on the face of the planet, the men of God, and we get no support. Christ said that, that we are without honor. And there are a lot of you who do help even though you’re not rich, and the fact that you care means more than anything. Your reward is with God.

“Ready to distribute”: ready to distribute to the men that are fighting to bring forth this nation. It’s your job. There are some who are going to help on the sideline, because these men put their lives on the line and at any time anything could go wrong with them. When the bishop was sick, we didn’t ask nobody for help. More people should have stepped up: you don’t know what his house is going through, what his family is going through; he needed around-the-clock care. White people set up GoFundMes; they don’t even have to know Tommy, they don’t have to know Billy Ray, all they need to know is a white man is sick, and they come out. They defend their covenant. Black people, forget about even asking them to send two dollars.

“Willing to communicate”: a lot of the people with money, like the celebrities, never communicate with us. That’s why I don’t exalt a celebrity who comes into the truth. You see them on Facebook with their fringes, posting Shalom; there’s a famous singer from a famous girl group people believe is in this truth, and I’m not going to say her name, because I don’t know if she wants her business out and because the Black Hebrew Israelites would start trying to hunt her down. You’re not willing to communicate with anyone in the truth; you’re giving attention to something we’ve been fighting our lives for, you’re not in no harm’s way, and you’re doing it just for show.

“Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation”: when you communicate with us and distribute to us, you’re laying up in store a good foundation for yourself. I’m not asking you, I’m not begging you. “Against the time to come”: times are going to get hard, and you may not be getting touched right now, but when the time comes for you to get touched, that’s what the Lord looks at. Did you help? Did you communicate? Did you see the men at war, or did you just sit back chilling? Even if you don’t want to help us, you should have it on record, when the angels check, who you helped. And you people who harmed others, I feel sorry for you when you cry out, because some of you came just to harm others, and you’ll be judged the same way. Some of you are rich and comfortable right now in order to help the others, and if you don’t, you’re not going to lay up a foundation.

There were a lot of celebrities watching who knew the bishop was going through things, and nobody sent a dime, nobody said they need help with medical expenses, while his family stopped work to help him. The Bible says charge them that are rich: if you got it and you’re not helping, to hell with you. I’d rather take the fifty cents, the dollar, the two dollars from the faithful people than beg the rich who sit back and watch, because your time is gonna come. You will have no foundation. You could be living good right now, and the Most High will turn it upside down from one day to the next. I’ve seen it with my own eyes.

precepts.why:
Christ covered it, that your reward is with God. “And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury”: it was customary to help the church, the treasury of the church. “And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.” What she gave wouldn’t put a dent in it; they wouldn’t even know whether she put it in or not. Look it up and two mites is like half a penny. People say, oh, I only had twenty dollars, I hope this helps get you lunch. No, that’s a big deal.

“Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all.” This woman with her two mites was better than what those rich men put in. Why? “For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings”: they’re not gonna feel it, they’ve got abundance, money coming in hand over fist, they’re good. “But she of her penury”: penury means extreme poverty; you don’t know when your next meal is coming. She “hath cast in all the living that she had”: she could die without resources, but her faith is so strong she says, I’m going to help the ministry out.

sense.text:
The question was what to do when you try to honor your parents according to the scriptures and they keep provoking you. You don’t disrespect them, but it comes to a point where you have to separate. If you don’t live with them, they should not be a problem to you.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers.” A lot of you do that: you see they’re unbelievers and you yoke yourselves to them. I honored my mother and I honored my father from a distance. They made it clear they wanted nothing to do with the scriptures, so I didn’t come and talk about it. My mother keeps doing this, my dad keeps doing this, but they’re not in my house, so I’m not going to yoke myself to them. If you’re in the house with them, that’s totally different.

The question was whether a man should leave his white wife that he has three children with after coming into the truth. The Bible says you’re not supposed to be married to a heathen, and if you stay with her you’re going to be judged. You’re obviously not reading your Bible.

“Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.” That is confirmation: judgment is coming, and whoever is sinning shall be destroyed out of this earth.

“And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease”: there are a lot of proud and arrogant people right now, but that is going to change. Some of y’all are living good. You have your nice white wives, you have your nice Chinese wives; not just white, it’s anybody outside. You’ve married outside of your nation, it’s all good for you, and you’re proud. “And will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.”
“I will make a man more precious than fine gold”: the Israelites are going to be changed.

“Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall remove out of her place, in the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.” That’s the nuclear war that’s coming. That’s Armageddon.

“And it shall be as the chased roe”: like when you’re hunting and going after a roe. Someone is going to be hunted. “And as a sheep that no man taketh up.”

“They shall every man turn to his own people, and flee every one into his own land.” The Lord is going to create conditions where it’s not going to be good to be married to a heathen.
“Every one that is found shall be thrust through”, meaning killed, “and every one that is joined unto them shall fall by the sword.”

“Their children also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled, and their wives ravished.” Things are going to get so bad that people are going to return back to their own people. What do they call America, AKA Babylon? A melting pot. That’s not the way God wanted things.

Right now people are arrogant, and they’ll say, are you telling me I have to leave my wife? I’m not telling you; that’s what the Bible said. If you don’t want to, stay there in your arrogance, but eventually judgment will catch up to you. The kids will still be preserved by God. Those kids are still Israelites, and as long as you’re walking in righteousness, don’t worry about her: the kids will still be preserved.

Asked whether it is a sin to take care of yourself when you don’t have a wife. “For I would that all men were even as I myself”: Paul had no wife, so he is saying, I wish that all you men could contain yourselves as me. “But every man hath his proper gift of God”: it’s a gift when you could serve the Lord and not desire companionship. “One after this manner, and another after that”: we all have different gifts. It’s a gift if you could be like, you know what, it’s not that big a deal to me, I’m just going to serve God by myself.

“I say therefore to the unmarried”: if you are unmarried, “and widows”: you’ve lost your spouse. “It is good for them if they abide even as I”, because Paul was by himself to do the work of God. It’ll be easier to serve God by yourself.

“But if they cannot contain”: you can’t contain because you have that desire and you don’t want to be lonely. “Let them marry”: nothing wrong with getting married. “For it is better to marry than to burn”: than to burn in lust.

So there’s nothing wrong either way. If you have the gift of celibacy and you can stay by yourself, fine, nobody’s going to attack you. If you can’t contain, you can marry.

Is it possible to completely stop sinning? It’s going to happen when Christ gets here; that’s when we’re going to get right. Right now there’s too many things that allow us to sin. This world is off course; this earth has to be rebuilt to God’s standards and his liking, and sin is everywhere.

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated, so that no man went through thee”: people hate us, we showed you that tonight. People want to get away from us. “I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations.”

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of kings: and thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.” “For brass I will bring gold”, “and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.” God is going to change these conditions for us.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: so you gangbangers that don’t care about each other and want to kill, you’re going to be eradicated. “Wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” The sun “shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

This is where it gets to the answer. “Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Verse 21 tells you that when God restructures the earth the way he wants, thy people also shall be all righteous. It’s not right now, because you’re in hell now. When God brings thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven, the people are going to be righteous.

Asked how a nurse is to apply it. “He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.” That was not for now; that was for the temple. There were laws of uncleanness for the temple. When you read Leviticus 15 it explains all different forms of uncleanliness, and there was a duration of time that you couldn’t defile the house of the Lord. That temple is destroyed, so that’s got nothing to do with right now.

How do you deal with not fitting in with the sisters, even when you try and haven’t offended anyone? It’s a big problem with a lot of you women. I’m not saying you, because I don’t know you, but I’m telling you what the Bible says. “Behold not every body’s beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.”

Who does that, who looks at everybody? Women. They size you up: your shoes, your hair, your nails, your dress. They’re looking for things, and if you don’t meet those standards they treat you funny: you don’t have makeup, you don’t have earrings, look at you, you’re fat, you’re skinny.

So a woman comes to this truth and tells me, I don’t know what’s wrong with the women in this school, they’re not nice to me. I tell them sit your ass down, that’s not what you’re here for, to be everybody’s friend. When the time comes for you to help the body and to let your light shine, you do it, but other than that don’t come here trying to be everybody’s friend. “Sit not in the midst of women.”

I will never tell you how to befriend women, because I don’t know how, and the Bible doesn’t say. It just warns you: don’t try to be that sister that always wants to be in the midst. Somehow the other sisters are going to have your name. They’re going to be looking at how you did this, how you did that, how you was with your kids, how you was over here. They’re going to watch you, you’re going to feel uncomfortable, and then you’re going to blame the church. You know how many women left IUIC blaming me for stuff that I don’t know what’s going on? So I stay out of women’s business, because they’re not here to learn; they’re doing exactly what the scripture says, and it’s something I cannot fix.

“For from garments cometh a moth”: a moth is always looking for a garment to attack, to bite, so he’s giving you that analogy. “And from women wickedness”: that’s why a lot of times women can’t get along. Women are messy. There’s a lot of women that are wicked; it took me some time to see that. So a lot of times when I interact with them it’s only to help them and keep it moving. When I come across a woman that’s loving and quiet, I pay more attention to her than that messy, wicked one with the loud Shalom before the storm.

“Better is the churlishness of a man than a courteous woman”: a churlish man is a mean man, and God said that’s better than a courteous woman. “A woman, I say, which bringeth shame and reproach.” She’s courteous, ‘Shalom, Most High in Christ bless,’ but she’s going to bring shame and reproach. Some women know how to work their way into your heart, into that circle, but when you get to meet them you’re like, yo, I didn’t know she was so obnoxious, so arrogant, so dismissive, so mean. The way you overlooked that is because she’s courteous. After you get to meet her you’re like, yo, I hate this girl. You give her a Shalom and you’re out, because you know some drama is attached to her.

precepts.why:
That’s why Paul had this written. “For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints”: God wants peace in all the churches, and this is the solution. “Let your women keep silence in the churches”: the best way to keep peace, Paul said, is for them to just be quiet. “For it is not permitted unto them.”

So Paul couldn’t give an answer to make the sisterhood and the unity work. It’s always some beef; they can’t even be in the kitchen without arguing, and that’s a shame, but that’s just the way these women are. In every office there’s always one: I don’t like what she said to me, I don’t like how she looked at me, I don’t think she likes me. Just stay over there, stay away from me.

Women are the best when they’re little and they just run up to you and you hug them and wish they could stay like that forever; they melt your heart. Then they grow up into somebody else and you’re like, yo, who is this person, she was just so sweet and loving. At some point they lose all of that. Then you get the ones that God has guiding them, and they grow up still pleasant to be around: you can have a conversation, you can talk with them, you can be yourself.

I’ve been in this truth a long time. I’ve tried to make sisters befriend each other and wondered why it’s not working, and then I realized the scripture is true: when you get a bunch of women together you get a bunch of issues. So my job is just to stay away from that. The sisters I am around are the ones who’ve shown good works: they’ve been loving, they’re kind, consistent, always pleasant, they always have good conversation, and I can let my guard down around them.

sense.text:
Asked to explain the scripture that says Esau is our brother and we are to respect him. “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother.” The Bible says to be at peace with all men, so we don’t teach y’all to hate white people here. God is going to judge them for what they’re doing. We created the conditions where they rule over us, so we don’t tell people to fight. There may be other camps that instruct you to fight with them and argue with them; we don’t teach you to fight the other nations.

We don’t teach to hate white people here, because that’s not what this movement is for. Getting rid of all the white people wouldn’t change what got us into the situation we’re in; white people are an outcome of it. So that has to be gotten rid of first, and we just be men and women of God; then we’ll deal with the other nations. Some Israelite camps focus their members to hate white people; we don’t do that here.

Someone said, sounds like you’re a product of your environment, you need to get the hell out of your environment. Let’s see if Christ agrees with that statement. “And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at meat in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him”. What type of people was Christ around? Publicans and sinners. So yes, I am a product of my environment: wherever the sinners are and the publicans that were hated, that is my environment, and Christ was not trying to get away from that.

Many Christian pastors remove themselves from that environment. Men of God, soldiers, warriors that lay down their life for their people as Christ did, surround themselves with people that are hated and sinners.

“And when the Pharisees saw it”: when the wicked leaders of the church saw it, “they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Because they never seen that before. They never seen a man surround himself with the worst people, the most despised people, the people that are hated, that have no hope.

“But when Jesus heard”: Jesus heard them talking behind his back. He “said unto them”, they that be whole “need not a physician”. That’s why T.D. Jakes and Creflo Dollar surround themselves with rich people with nice white picket fences and six-figure jobs; they’re not letting those sinners come around them. “But they that are sick”: the people that are sick is where you’re going to find me. I’m not looking for a place of comfort.

“But go ye and learn what that meaneth”: that’s my answer to people who say I’m a product of my environment. Go ye and learn what that means: “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice”. I’m where I am because the people need mercy; no one has shown them mercy. I could easily pick up and abandon them, but a real man of God won’t do that.

Does God still speak to us in dreams, and how do we translate them? There’s no scripture that says how to translate them; it tells you not even to. “The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.” If you pay too much attention to your dreams, it’ll make you into a fool.

“Whoso regardeth dreams”: if you’re putting a lot of regard to your dreams, it’s “like him that catcheth at a shadow”: you cannot catch a shadow. “And followeth after the wind”: you cannot follow the wind. So the Bible tells us not to pay attention to our dreams to that extent.

I have bad dreams every single night; I don’t know what it’s like to have a good dream. Those dreams could be sent from God to keep me the way that I am, because the Lord can interfere with your dreams, but I don’t let them alter my understanding.

“The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another”: your dream cannot always mean what you think it is. “Even as the likeness of a face to a face”: you see a face and it looks like somebody else, but it’s not.

“Of an unclean thing what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false what truth can come?” Some of your dreams are false; there’s no truth to them. So the Bible doesn’t tell us how to interpret dreams, but dreams can be sent to us from God to alter our understanding to the way he wants it.

My mom used to go to sleep and wake up, I dreamed about fish, let me get my dream book and see what number I should play for fishes. Mom, you was probably hungry. She’d spend hundreds of dollars with that stupid ass dream book, out in her house slippers and her damn robe trying to get the number in before a certain time. When I read this scripture and tried to show it to her, she wouldn’t listen: I dreamed the dog was licking my foot, let me see what this says in my dream book.

Whoever comes into the wilderness after the judgment on this earth with the same spirit they have now is going to die. Christ is going to deliver some of you just to make examples of you in the wilderness. A nuclear war is coming, and God is going to deliver us from the fire and drop us some place where there is no fire, the wilderness. Don’t come into that place with your same mindset, because he says ‘I will purge out the rebels’. Some of you are rebellious to this word. You have a chance now; you could be like, I hate Deacon Asaph, he makes me sick. In the wilderness you’re not going to be able to do that; you will be put to death instantly. Even after being taken in the chariot of God, people will still rebel, and they’re going to be put to death.

“As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you: And I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered”. God is going to deliver us from the lands of our captivity.

“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people”, because God has a place of protection for us, “and there will I plead with you face to face.” So you will not be calling me or him out of his name anymore, and you will not be acting like that anymore. You will not be in the wilderness with your pants hanging off your ass. Black woman, you will not have long eyelashes that look like they can touch me before you greet me; you will not have blonde hair with weave on. It’s going to be a whole bunch of reformation there.

“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. How did he plead with them before? He sent snakes to bite that ass up; a lot of people died in the wilderness. So that’s going to be a repeat of that. It’s not going to be like now, where you just be like, ah, let me listen to what he’s talking about on Friday. You’re going to get your ass whooped in the wilderness, bad.
“And I will cause you to pass under the rod”, “I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: meaning you’re going to get corrected or rejected once your wickedness is detected.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. Some of you are still going to be trying to challenge Christ and the prophets; the only difference is we’re going to have big boots. You’re going to get a foot in that ass; it’s going to be so spectacular, because we can’t get you now, but then we’re going to get you. “I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn, and they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.” Negroes will be gone in that day; it’s going to be glorious.

Some of you are going to get delivered only to be destroyed, because he needs some crash test dummies, so y’all be like, yo, don’t play with this man. Tyrone was running his mouth and all of a sudden his lips hit the floor; we didn’t even see when Christ put the sword back in. If Peter could chop off a centurion’s ear, you don’t think he could chop up somebody’s lips? So some of you Negroes exist only to get judgment later on. That’s why I don’t mind the Negroes: let them talk. You wicked Israelites in other groups, you stay there; you don’t know this Bible, you don’t know what you’re being lined up for. If you was hating men now teaching the word, you think you’re going to come in the wilderness and get a pass?
